sanskrit: madhye kṛtvā tu rājānaṃ bhīmasenārjunāv ubhau niṣīdatur mahātmānau ślakṣṇayor maṇipīṭhayoḥ
english: Placing the king between them, the two great-souled ones, Bhīmasena and Arjuna, seated themselves upon two smooth jewelled stools.

sanskrit: dānte śayyāsane śubhre jāmbūnadavibhūṣite pṛthāpi sahadevena sahāste nakulena ca
english: Upon a bright ivory couch-seat adorned with Jāmbūnada gold, Pṛthā too sat together with Sahadeva and Nakula.

sanskrit: sudharmā viduro dhaumyo dhṛtarāṣṭraś ca kauravaḥ niṣedur jvalanākāreṣv āsaneṣu pṛthak pṛthak
english: Sudharman, Vidura, Dhaumya, and Dhṛtarāṣṭra of the Kuru line seated themselves, each upon a separate seat blazing like fire.

sanskrit: yuyutsuḥ saṃjayaś caiva gāndhārī ca yaśasvinī dhṛtarāṣṭro yato rājā tataḥ sarva upāviśan
english: Yuyutsu, Saṃjaya, and the renowned Gāndhārī—all of them took their places there where King Dhṛtarāṣṭra sat.

sanskrit: tatropaviṣṭo dharmātmā śvetāḥ sumanaso 'spṛśat svastikān akṣatān bhūmiṃ suvarṇaṃ rajataṃ maṇīn
english: Seated there, the righteous one touched white flowers, svastika emblems, unbroken grains, the earth, gold, silver, and gems.

sanskrit: tataḥ prakṛtayaḥ sarvāḥ puraskṛtya purohitam dadṛśur dharmarājānam ādāya bahu maṅgalam
english: Then all the subjects, placing the household priest at their head, came bearing many auspicious offerings to behold the king of righteousness.

sanskrit: pṛthivīṃ ca suvarṇaṃ ca ratnāni vividhāni ca ābhiṣecanikaṃ bhāṇḍaṃ sarvasaṃbhārasaṃbhṛtam
english: They brought earth and gold and jewels of many kinds, and the consecration-vessel filled with every requisite for the rite.

sanskrit: kāñcanaudumbarās tatra rājatāḥ pṛthivīmayāḥ pūrṇakumbhāḥ sumanaso lājā barhīṃṣi gorasāḥ
english: There were full jars of gold, of udumbara wood, of silver, and of earthenware, with flowers, parched grain, kuśa grass, and milk-curds.

sanskrit: śamīpalāśapuṃnāgāḥ samidho madhusarpiṣī sruva audumbaraḥ śaṅkhās tathā hemavibhūṣitāḥ
english: There were kindling-sticks of śamī, palāśa, and puṃnāga wood, honey and clarified butter, a ladle of udumbara wood, and conches adorned with gold.

sanskrit: dāśārheṇābhyanujñātas tatra dhaumyaḥ purohitaḥ prāgudakpravaṇāṃ vedīṃ lakṣaṇenopalipya ha
english: Authorized by the Dāśārha, the household priest Dhaumya there smeared and consecrated by the prescribed marks an altar sloping toward the northeast.

sanskrit: vyāghracarmottare ślakṣṇe sarvatobhadra āsane dṛḍhapādapratiṣṭhāne hutāśanasamatviṣi
english: Upon a smooth seat covered over with a tiger's skin, auspicious on every side, firm-footed and steady, shining bright as the oblation-eating fire,

sanskrit: upaveśya mahātmānaṃ kṛṣṇāṃ ca drupadātmajām juhāva pāvakaṃ dhīmān vidhimantrapuraskṛtam
english: having seated the great-souled one and Kṛṣṇā, the daughter of Drupada, the wise priest offered into the purifying fire with rite and mantra duly observed.

sanskrit: abhyaṣiñcat patiṃ pṛthvyāḥ kuntīputraṃ yudhiṣṭhiram dhṛtarāṣṭraś ca rājarṣiḥ sarvāḥ prakṛtayas tathā
english: He consecrated Yudhiṣṭhira, son of Kuntī, as lord of the earth; and so did the royal sage Dhṛtarāṣṭra and all the subjects.

sanskrit: tato 'nuvādayām āsuḥ paṇavānakadundubhīḥ dharmarājo 'pi tat sarvaṃ pratijagrāha dharmataḥ
english: Then they caused cymbals, drums, and kettledrums to resound; and the king of righteousness accepted all of it according to the law.

sanskrit: pūjayām āsa tāṃś cāpi vidhivad bhūridakṣiṇaḥ tato niṣkasahasreṇa brāhmaṇān svasti vācayat vedādhyayanasaṃpannāñ śīlavṛttasamanvitān
english: And, generous with abundant gifts, he honored them all according to the ordinance; then with a thousand gold pieces he had the brāhmaṇas pronounce blessings—those accomplished in Vedic study and endowed with good character and conduct.

sanskrit: te prītā brāhmaṇā rājan svasty ūcur jayam eva ca haṃsā iva ca nardantaḥ praśaśaṃsur yudhiṣṭhiram
english: Well pleased, O king, the brāhmaṇas pronounced blessing and victory, and, crying out like swans, they extolled Yudhiṣṭhira:

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira mahābāho diṣṭyā jayasi pāṇḍava diṣṭyā svadharmaṃ prāpto 'si vikrameṇa mahādyute
english: "Mighty-armed Yudhiṣṭhira, son of Pāṇḍu, by good fortune you are victorious! By good fortune, O greatly radiant one, you have attained your own dharma by your valor.

sanskrit: diṣṭyā gāṇḍīvadhanvā ca bhīmasenaś ca pāṇḍavaḥ tvaṃ cāpi kuśalī rājan mādrīputrau ca pāṇḍavau
english: By good fortune the wielder of the Gāṇḍīva and Bhīmasena son of Pāṇḍu, and you too, O king, are well, and the two Pāṇḍava sons of Mādrī as well.

sanskrit: muktā vīrakṣayād asmāt saṃgrāmān nihatadviṣaḥ kṣipram uttarakālāni kuru kāryāṇi pāṇḍava
english: Delivered from this slaughter of heroes, your foes slain in battle, swiftly now, O son of Pāṇḍu, perform the duties that the time to come requires."

sanskrit: tataḥ pratyarcitaḥ sadbhir dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ pratipede mahad rājyaṃ suhṛdbhiḥ saha bhārata
english: Then, honored in return by the virtuous, Yudhiṣṭhira the king of righteousness took possession of the great kingdom together with his friends, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca prakṛtīnāṃ tu tad vākyaṃ deśakālopasaṃhitam śrutvā yudhiṣṭhiro rājāthottaraṃ pratyabhāṣata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard that speech of the subjects, fitting to the place and the time, King Yudhiṣṭhira then spoke this reply in answer.

sanskrit: dhanyāḥ pāṇḍusutā loke yeṣāṃ brāhmaṇapuṃgavāḥ tathyān vāpy atha vātathyān guṇān āhuḥ samāgatāḥ
english: "Blessed in the world are the sons of Pāṇḍu, whose virtues—whether truly theirs or not—the foremost of brāhmaṇas, gathered here, proclaim.

sanskrit: anugrāhyā vayaṃ nūnaṃ bhavatām iti me matiḥ yatraivaṃ guṇasaṃpannān asmān brūtha vimatsarāḥ
english: Surely we are worthy of your favor—such is my conviction—since, free of envy, you call us thus endowed with merit.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭro mahārājaḥ pitā no daivataṃ param sāśane 'sya priye caiva stheyaṃ matpriyakāṅkṣibhiḥ
english: The great king Dhṛtarāṣṭra is our father and our highest deity; those who wish my pleasure must abide by his command and his good will.

sanskrit: etadarthaṃ hi jīvāmi kṛtvā jñātivadhaṃ mahat asya śuśrūṣaṇaṃ kāryaṃ mayā nityam atandriṇā
english: For this very purpose I go on living, after having wrought the great slaughter of my kinsmen: that I, ever unwearied, must render him service.

sanskrit: yadi cāham anugrāhyo bhavatāṃ suhṛdāṃ tataḥ dhṛtarāṣṭre yathāpūrvaṃ vṛttiṃ vartitum arhatha
english: And if I am worthy of the favor of you, my friends, then toward Dhṛtarāṣṭra you ought to conduct yourselves just as before.

sanskrit: eṣa nātho hi jagato bhavatāṃ ca mayā saha asyaiva pṛthivī kṛtsnā pāṇḍavāḥ sarva eva ca etan manasi kartavyaṃ bhavadbhir vacanaṃ mama
english: For he is the lord of the world, of you, and of myself; to him alone belongs the whole earth, and the Pāṇḍavas one and all. This word of mine you must take to heart.

sanskrit: anugamya ca rājānaṃ yatheṣṭaṃ gamyatām iti paurajānapadān sarvān visṛjya kurunandanaḥ yauvarājyena kauravyo bhīmasenam ayojayat
english: "Having attended upon the king, go now as you please." So dismissing all the townsfolk and country-folk, the joy of the Kurus, scion of the Kauravas, appointed Bhīmasena to the office of heir-apparent.

sanskrit: mantre ca niścaye caiva ṣāḍguṇyasya ca cintane viduraṃ buddhisaṃpannaṃ prītimān vai samādiśat
english: For counsel and decision and the deliberation of the sixfold policy of state, he gladly appointed Vidura, who was perfect in wisdom.

sanskrit: kṛtākṛtaparijñāne tathāyavyayacintane saṃjayaṃ yojayām āsa ṛddham ṛddhair guṇair yutam
english: To the oversight of what was done and left undone, and to the reckoning of income and expenditure, he assigned Saṃjaya, prosperous and endowed with abundant virtues.

sanskrit: balasya parimāṇe ca bhaktavetanayos tathā nakulaṃ vyādiśad rājā karmiṇām anvavekṣaṇe
english: To the mustering of the army, the rations and the wages, and the supervision of the workmen, the king assigned Nakula.

sanskrit: paracakroparodhe ca dṛptānāṃ cāvamardane yudhiṣṭhiro mahārājaḥ phalgunaṃ vyādideśa ha
english: To the repelling of hostile armies and the crushing of the insolent, the great king Yudhiṣṭhira appointed Phalguna.

sanskrit: dvijānāṃ vedakāryeṣu kāryeṣv anyeṣu caiva hi dhaumyaṃ purodhasāṃ śreṣṭhaṃ vyādideśa paraṃtapaḥ
english: To the Vedic rites of the twice-born and to other sacred duties, the scorcher of foes appointed Dhaumya, the best of household priests.

sanskrit: sahadevaṃ samīpasthaṃ nityam eva samādiśat tena gopyo hi nṛpatiḥ sarvāvastho viśāṃ pate
english: Sahadeva he appointed to remain ever at his side; for by him the king was to be guarded in every circumstance, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: yān yān amanyad yogyāṃś ca yeṣu yeṣv iha karmasu tāṃs tāṃs teṣv eva yuyuje prīyamāṇo mahīpatiḥ
english: Whomever he judged fit for whatever tasks, to those very tasks the lord of earth, well pleased, appointed them.

sanskrit: viduraṃ saṃjayaṃ caiva yuyutsuṃ ca mahāmatim abravīt paravīraghno dharmātmā dharmavatsalaḥ
english: To Vidura, Saṃjaya, and the great-minded Yuyutsu, the slayer of enemy heroes, righteous-souled and devoted to dharma, spoke thus:

sanskrit: utthāyotthāya yat kāryam asya rājñaḥ pitur mama sarvaṃ bhavadbhiḥ kartavyam apramattair yathātatham
english: "Whatever needs to be done from one occasion to the next for this king, my father, all of it you must accomplish, vigilant and exactly as is fitting.

sanskrit: paurajānapadānāṃ ca yāni kāryāṇi nityaśaḥ rājānaṃ samanujñāpya tāni kāryāṇi dharmataḥ
english: And whatever affairs of the townsfolk and country-folk arise from day to day, those you must, with the king's leave, attend to according to the law."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato yudhiṣṭhiro rājā jñātīnāṃ ye hatā mṛdhe śrāddhāni kārayām āsa teṣāṃ pṛthag udāradhīḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then King Yudhiṣṭhira, noble of mind, had the śrāddha rites performed, each separately, for those of his kinsmen who had fallen in the battle.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭro dadau rājā putrāṇām aurdhvadehikam sarvakāmaguṇopetam annaṃ gāś ca dhanāni ca ratnāni ca vicitrāṇi mahārhāṇi mahāyaśāḥ
english: King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, of great renown, gave for his sons the funeral offerings, complete with every desirable thing—food, cattle, wealth, and jewels of varied kinds and great worth.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiras tu karṇasya droṇasya ca mahātmanaḥ dhṛṣṭadyumnābhimanyubhyāṃ haiḍimbasya ca rakṣasaḥ
english: And Yudhiṣṭhira, for Karṇa and for the great-souled Droṇa, for Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Abhimanyu, and for the rākṣasa son of Hiḍimbā,

sanskrit: virāṭaprabhṛtīnāṃ ca suhṛdām upakāriṇām drupadadraupadeyānāṃ draupadyā sahito dadau
english: and for Virāṭa and the rest of his helpful friends, and for Drupada and the sons of Draupadī—together with Draupadī he made the offerings.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇānāṃ sahasrāṇi pṛthag ekaikam uddiśan dhanaiś ca vastrai ratnaiś ca gobhiś ca samatarpayat
english: Designating thousands of brāhmaṇas, each one singly in turn, he gratified them with wealth and garments, with jewels and with cattle.

sanskrit: ye cānye pṛthivīpālā yeṣāṃ nāsti suhṛjjanaḥ uddiśyoddiśya teṣāṃ ca cakre rājaurdhvadaihikam
english: And for those other rulers of earth who had no kinsfolk left to them, the king, naming each one, performed the rites for the dead.

sanskrit: sabhāḥ prapāś ca vividhās taḍāgāni ca pāṇḍavaḥ suhṛdāṃ kārayām āsa sarveṣām aurdhvadaihikam
english: Assembly-halls and many watering-stations and tanks the son of Pāṇḍu caused to be made as funerary memorials for all his friends.

sanskrit: sa teṣām anṛṇo bhūtvā gatvā lokeṣv avācyatām kṛtakṛtyo 'bhavad rājā prajā dharmeṇa pālayan
english: Thus freed of his debt to them, and having attained beyond reproach among the worlds, the king became one who had fulfilled his duty, governing his subjects with righteousness.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ yathāpūrvaṃ gāndhārīṃ viduraṃ tathā sarvāṃś ca kauravāmātyān bhṛtyāṃś ca samapūjayat
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra as before, and Gāndhārī and Vidura likewise, and all the Kaurava ministers and retainers, he honored fittingly.

sanskrit: yāś ca tatra striyaḥ kāś cid dhatavīrā hatātmajāḥ sarvās tāḥ kauravo rājā saṃpūjyāpālayad ghṛṇī
english: And whatever women there were whose heroes were slain, whose sons were slain, all of them the compassionate Kaurava king honored and protected.

sanskrit: dīnāndhakṛpaṇānāṃ ca gṛhācchādanabhojanaiḥ ānṛśaṃsyaparo rājā cakārānugrahaṃ prabhuḥ
english: And to the wretched, the blind, and the helpless, with houses, clothing, and food, the king, devoted to kindness, the sovereign, showed his grace.

sanskrit: sa vijitya mahīṃ kṛtsnām ānṛṇyaṃ prāpya vairiṣu niḥsapatnaḥ sukhī rājā vijahāra yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Having conquered the whole earth and discharged his debt against his foes, King Yudhiṣṭhira, without a rival and at ease, dwelt in contentment.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca abhiṣikto mahāprājño rājyaṃ prāpya yudhiṣṭhiraḥ dāśārhaṃ puṇḍarīkākṣam uvāca prāñjaliḥ śuciḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Consecrated and having gained the kingdom, the greatly wise Yudhiṣṭhira, purified and with palms joined, spoke to the lotus-eyed Dāśārha:

sanskrit: tava kṛṣṇa prasādena nayena ca balena ca buddhyā ca yaduśārdūla tathā vikramaṇena ca
english: "By your grace, O Kṛṣṇa, by your statecraft and your strength, by your wisdom, O tiger of the Yadus, and by your valor,

sanskrit: punaḥ prāptam idaṃ rājyaṃ pitṛpaitāmahaṃ mayā namas te puṇḍarīkākṣa punaḥ punar ariṃdama
english: this kingdom of my fathers and forefathers has been regained by me. Homage to you, O lotus-eyed one, again and again, O subduer of foes!

sanskrit: tvām ekam āhuḥ puruṣaṃ tvām āhuḥ sātvatāṃ patim nāmabhis tvāṃ bahuvidhaiḥ stuvanti paramarṣayaḥ
english: You alone they call the Puruṣa; you they call the lord of the Sātvatas; with names of many kinds the supreme sages praise you.

sanskrit: viśvakarman namas te 'stu viśvātman viśvasaṃbhava viṣṇo jiṣṇo hare kṛṣṇa vaikuṇṭha puruṣottama
english: Maker of all, homage be to you; Soul of all, source of all—Viṣṇu, Jiṣṇu, Hari, Kṛṣṇa, Vaikuṇṭha, supreme among beings!

sanskrit: adityāḥ saptarātraṃ tu purāṇe garbhatāṃ gataḥ pṛśnigarbhas tvam evaikas triyugaṃ tvāṃ vadanty api
english: In the ancient age you entered the womb of Aditi for seven nights; you alone are the child of Pṛśni, and they call you also Triyuga, he of the three ages.

sanskrit: śuciśravā hṛṣīkeśo ghṛtārcir haṃsa ucyase tricakṣuḥ śambhur ekas tvaṃ vibhur dāmodaro 'pi ca
english: You are called Śuciśravas, Hṛṣīkeśa, Ghṛtārci, and Haṃsa; three-eyed, you are the one Śambhu, the all-pervading, and Dāmodara as well.

sanskrit: varāho 'gnir bṛhadbhānur vṛṣaṇas tārkṣyalakṣaṇaḥ anīkasāhaḥ puruṣaḥ śipiviṣṭa urukramaḥ
english: You are the Boar, Agni, Bṛhadbhānu of mighty radiance, the bull Vṛṣaṇa, marked by the emblem of Tārkṣya; the vanquisher of armies, the Puruṣa, Śipiviṣṭa, the wide-striding one.

sanskrit: vāciṣṭha ugraḥ senānīḥ satyo vājasanir guhaḥ acyutaś cyāvano 'rīṇāṃ saṃkṛtir vikṛtir vṛṣaḥ
english: Lord of speech, the terrible, the army-leader, the true one, giver of food and strength, the hidden one; the unfallen, the overthrower of foes, the maker and unmaker, the bull.

sanskrit: kṛtavartmā tvam evādrir vṛṣagarbho vṛṣākapiḥ sindhukṣid ūrmis trikakut tridhāmā trivṛd acyutaḥ
english: You are Kṛtavartman, you are the Mountain, Vṛṣagarbha, Vṛṣākapi; dweller in the sea, the Wave, the three-peaked, threefold-abode, threefold, the unfallen.

sanskrit: samrāḍ virāṭ svarāṭ caiva surarāḍ dharmado bhavaḥ vibhur bhūr abhibhūḥ kṛṣṇaḥ kṛṣṇavartmā tvam eva ca
english: Sovereign, the vast, the self-ruling, and king of the gods; giver of dharma, the becoming; the all-pervading, the Earth, the all-surpassing, Kṛṣṇa, and the one whose path is dark-tracked—that too are you.

sanskrit: sviṣṭakṛd bhiṣagāvartaḥ kapilas tvaṃ ca vāmanaḥ yajño dhruvaḥ pataṃgaś ca jayatsenas tvam ucyase
english: The doer of right sacrifice, the healer, the Whirlpool, Kapila, and the Dwarf are you; the Sacrifice, the steadfast, the Bird, and Jayatsena—so you are called.

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍī nahuṣo babhrur divaspṛk tvaṃ punarvasuḥ subabhrur ukṣo rukmas tvaṃ suṣeṇo dundubhis tathā
english: Śikhaṇḍin, Nahuṣa, Babhru, you are the toucher of heaven, Punarvasu; Subabhru, the Ox, Rukma are you, Suṣeṇa, and likewise the Drum.

sanskrit: gabhastinemiḥ śrīpadmaṃ puṣkaraṃ puṣpadhāraṇaḥ ṛbhur vibhuḥ sarvasūkṣmas tvaṃ sāvitraṃ ca paṭhyase
english: Rim of the sunbeams, the radiant Lotus, the Lotus-flower, the bearer of flowers; the Ṛbhu, the all-pervading, subtlest of all are you, and as the Sāvitra hymn you are recited.

sanskrit: ambhonidhis tvaṃ brahmā tvaṃ pavitraṃ dhāma dhanva ca hiraṇyagarbhaṃ tvām āhuḥ svadhā svāhā ca keśava
english: You are the ocean of waters, you are Brahmā, the purifying, the abode, and the bow; they call you Hiraṇyagarbha, the Svadhā and the Svāhā, O Keśava.

sanskrit: yonis tvam asya pralayaś ca kṛṣṇa; tvam evedaṃ sṛjasi viśvam agre viśvaṃ cedaṃ tvadvaśe viśvayone; namo 'stu te śārṅgacakrāsipāṇe
english: You are the womb of this all and its dissolution, O Kṛṣṇa; you alone bring forth this universe in the beginning, and this universe lies under your sway, O womb of all. Homage be to you, who bear in your hands the Śārṅga bow, the discus, and the sword!

sanskrit: evaṃ stuto dharmarājena kṛṣṇaḥ; sabhāmadhye prītimān puṣkarākṣaḥ tam abhyanandad bhārataṃ puṣkalābhir; vāgbhir jyeṣṭhaṃ pāṇḍavaṃ yādavāgryaḥ
english: Praised thus by the king of righteousness in the midst of the assembly, the lotus-eyed Kṛṣṇa, well pleased, the foremost of the Yādavas, greeted that Bhārata, the eldest son of Pāṇḍu, with words full and gracious.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato visarjayām āsa sarvāḥ prakṛtayo nṛpaḥ viviśuś cābhyanujñātā yathāsvāni gṛhāṇi ca
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then the king dismissed all his subjects, and, given leave, they returned each to his own dwelling.

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiro rājā bhīmaṃ bhīmaparākramam sāntvayann abravīd dhīmān arjunaṃ yamajau tathā
english: Then the wise King Yudhiṣṭhira, comforting Bhīma of terrible prowess, and Arjuna, and the twins, spoke to them:

sanskrit: śatrubhir vividhaiḥ śastraiḥ kṛttadehā mahāraṇe śrāntā bhavantaḥ subhṛśaṃ tāpitāḥ śokamanyubhiḥ
english: "Your bodies hacked by the enemy with weapons of every kind in the great battle, you have grown utterly weary, sorely tormented by grief and wrath.

sanskrit: araṇye duḥkhavasatīr matkṛte puruṣottamāḥ bhavadbhir anubhūtāś ca yathā kupuruṣais tathā
english: On my account, O best of men, you endured wretched dwellings in the forest, as though you were base-born men.

sanskrit: yathāsukhaṃ yathājoṣaṃ jayo 'yam anubhūyatām viśrāntāṃl labdhavijñānāñ śvaḥ sametāsmi vaḥ punaḥ
english: Now enjoy this victory at your ease and to your heart's content; rested and recollected, tomorrow I shall meet with you again."

sanskrit: tato duryodhanagṛhaṃ prāsādair upaśobhitam bahuratnasamākīrṇaṃ dāsīdāsasamākulam
english: Then the palace of Duryodhana, graced with lofty mansions, strewn with many jewels and thronged with serving-women and serving-men,

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭrābhyanujñātaṃ bhrātrā dattaṃ vṛkodaraḥ pratipede mahābāhur mandaraṃ maghavān iva
english: sanctioned by Dhṛtarāṣṭra and bestowed by his brother, the mighty-armed Vṛkodara took into his possession, as Maghavat took Mount Mandara.

sanskrit: yathā duryodhanagṛhaṃ tathā duḥśāsanasya ca prāsādamālāsaṃyuktaṃ hematoraṇabhūṣitam
english: And as with Duryodhana's palace, so with Duḥśāsana's, ringed with rows of mansions and adorned with golden archways,

sanskrit: dāsīdāsasusaṃpūrṇaṃ prabhūtadhanadhānyavat pratipede mahābāhur arjuno rājaśāsanāt
english: filled with serving-women and serving-men and abounding in wealth and grain—the mighty-armed Arjuna took into his possession by the king's command.

sanskrit: durmarṣaṇasya bhavanaṃ duḥśāsanagṛhād varam kuberabhavanaprakhyaṃ maṇihemavibhūṣitam
english: The dwelling of Durmarṣaṇa, finer than the house of Duḥśāsana, resembling the palace of Kubera and adorned with gems and gold,

sanskrit: nakulāya varārhāya karśitāya mahāvane dadau prīto mahārāja dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: the king of righteousness, Yudhiṣṭhira, well pleased, O great king, gave to Nakula, worthy of the best, who had been worn thin in the great forest.

sanskrit: durmukhasya ca veśmāgryaṃ śrīmat kanakabhūṣitam pūrṇaṃ padmadalākṣīṇāṃ strīṇāṃ śayanasaṃkulam
english: And the splendid foremost mansion of Durmukha, gold-adorned, full of women with eyes like lotus-petals and crowded with couches,

sanskrit: pradadau sahadevāya satataṃ priyakāriṇe mumude tac ca labdhvā sa kailāsaṃ dhanado yathā
english: he bestowed upon Sahadeva, ever the doer of his pleasure; and receiving it, he rejoiced as the giver of wealth rejoiced in gaining Kailāsa.
